body: I can reproduce in 4.7 dev 2 using the offical binaries with `Forward+` and `Mobile`. But when i compile by myself (with `dev_build=yes` or `production=yes` with both MSVC or MinGW) no crash or error happens and nothing appears on the screen.

I could observe the same behavior today when I wanted to dig a bit deeper into the issue. I am only getting the error(s) and crash with the official binaries (4.7 dev2). Using a self-compiled version of the engine (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/778cf54dabd8a9e25b698a87036ab8604183f303 compiled using MSVC with `dev_build=yes`) does not show any error and does not crash, but the generated texture is not visible.

I looked at the issue using the D3D12 debug layer and the first error apparently comes from a missing usage bit on the texture:

```
D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandList::ResourceBarrier: D3D12_RESOURCE_STATES (D3D12_RESOURCE_STATE_RENDER_TARGET) has bits that mismatch support required from D3D12_RESOURCE_FLAGS (D3D12_RESOURCE_FLAG_ALLOW_UNORDERED_ACCESS). Missing required flags: (D3D12_RESOURCE_FLAG_ALLOW_RENDER_TARGET). Set prohibited flags: (D3D12_RESOURCE_FLAG_NONE). [ RESOURCE_MANIPULATION ERROR #524: RESOURCE_BARRIER_MISMATCHING_MISC_FLAGS]
```

When setting `TEXTURE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT`, the code executes without crashes, does not show errors in the console, but the compute shader still does not run correctly (4.7 dev2, official binaries).
I get the following errors from the D3D12 debug layer when the compute shader is executed:

```
D3D12 ERROR: CGraphicsCommandList::SetComputeRootDescriptorTable: Specified GPU Descriptor Handle (ptr = 0x2317adcf061 at 0 offsetInDescriptorsFromDescriptorHeapStart), for Root Signature (0x00000231782F59A0:'RID:4307852197888')'s Descriptor Table (at Parameter Index [0])'s Descriptor Range (at Range Index [0] of type D3D12_DESCRIPTOR_RANGE_TYPE_UAV) has an underlying stale or released resource is invalid for use. [ EXECUTION ERROR #1042: DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE_WITH_INVALID_RESOURCE]
D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandList::Close: An ID3D12Resource object (0x000002317878FFC0:'RID:4316442132520'), referenced in the command list being closed (0x0000023172349C90:'Unnamed ID3D12GraphicsCommandList Object'), was deleted prior to closing the command list.  This is invalid and can result in application instability. [ EXECUTION ERROR #921: OBJECT_DELETED_WHILE_STILL_IN_USE]
D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandQueue1::ExecuteCommandLists: An ID3D12Resource object (0x000002317878FFC0:'RID:4316442132520') referenced in a command list (0x00000231723526C0:'Unnamed ID3D12GraphicsCommandList Object') was deleted prior to executing the command list.  This is invalid and can result in application instability. [ EXECUTION ERROR #921: OBJECT_DELETED_WHILE_STILL_IN_USE]
D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandQueue1::ExecuteCommandLists: Barrier layout(D3D12_BARRIER_LAYOUT_LEGACY_COPY_DEST), pResource = 0x000002317878CDB0:'RID:4342211936298', subresource = [0], does not match expected layout (D3D12_BARRIER_LAYOUT_COMMON) using D3D12_COMMAND_LIST_TYPE_COPY command list 0x000002316FE60420:'Unnamed ID3D12GraphicsCommandList Object') in CopyTextureRegion for use as a destination resource [ STATE_SETTING ERROR #1334: INCOMPATIBLE_BARRIER_LAYOUT]
D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandQueue1::ExecuteCommandLists: Barrier layout(D3D12_BARRIER_LAYOUT_LEGACY_COPY_DEST), pResource = 0x0000023178792120:'RID:4355096838188', subresource = [0], does not match expected layout (D3D12_BARRIER_LAYOUT_COMMON) using D3D12_COMMAND_LIST_TYPE_COPY command list 0x000002316FE60420:'Unnamed ID3D12GraphicsCommandList Object') in CopyTextureRegion for use as a destination resource [ STATE_SETTING ERROR #1334: INCOMPATIBLE_BARRIER_LAYOUT]
```

The last two errors are likely unrelated to the issue, as I also get them when running the compute shader on the main RD, where there is no `texture_create_from_extension()` involved and the compute shader produces the expected result.

You're not using this API correctly. Vulkan appearing correct is complete luck because the VVL complains about it:

```cpp
.\drivers/vulkan/rendering_context_driver_vulkan.cpp:649 - VALIDATION - Message Id Number: -1075942427 | Message Id Name: VUID-vkCreateImageView-image-09179
	vkCreateImageView(): pCreateInfo->image (VkImage 0x7390000000739) was created, allocated or retrieved from VkDevice 0x223f51a9d80, but command is using (or its dispatchable parameter is associated with) VkDevice 0x266bfd62270
The Vulkan spec states: VkImageViewCreateInfo::image must have been created from device (https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/resources.html#VUID-vkCreateImageView-image-09179)
	Objects - 2
		Object[0] - VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE, Handle 2640328401520
		Object[1] - VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE, Handle 2353459273088
```

The native handles are supposed to come from the same underlying device the RDD is assigned to.
Makes sense after reading the Vulkan API documentation, should have looked into it earlier. Thanks!
